findings.text: All four options say “only”, but the Inca empire also covered parts of Bolivia and Colombia, so even D is incomplete. Dropping “only” would fix it.

The key calls Dhanvantari the “Father of Indian Medicine”, a title usually given to Charaka. Q15 also lists Charaka as a Gupta-period scientist, while most historians place him in the Kushana period. The key follows the state textbook; a note in the book would help students who meet the other view.
Q48 and Q56 ask the same thing (the Latin word “colere”).
Option D repeats “vi” (“i, ii, vi, v and vi”). The key (C) is right.
The statements are numbered i–iv, but the options refer to A, B, C and D. Statement ii (more national income means more per capita income) is not always true, since it depends on population.

Both questions ask which water body is the saltiest, and the key gives Lake Van (C) both times. That follows the textbook’s figure of 330 ppt for Lake Van, but Lake Van’s measured salinity is about 22 ppt. The Dead Sea, at about 340 ppt, is far saltier, so the answer is A. The same question is printed twice.
Statement A is garbled (“…is 180° longitude it is short detours in order”) and is hard to judge as printed. The key is A.
Option A is missing (the options start at B), and the wording of B–D (“not complementary”, “irrational”, “proportional”) is hard to follow. The key is D.

None of the pairs is a correct rock change. Granite turns into gneiss, sandstone into quartzite and limestone into marble. Graphite → diamond (the key, D) is a change of mineral under pressure, not a metamorphic rock.
Stromboli (the key, B) is active, but so is Krakatoa: Anak Krakatau erupted in 2018 and after. Replacing Krakatoa with a dormant or extinct volcano would leave one answer.
As printed, 3 − 4(3 − 4) − 1 = 6, so the value is 1/6, which is not an option. The key’s 1/7 needs the “−1” to be an index on (3 − 4): [3 − 4(3 − 4)⁻¹]⁻¹ = (3 + 4)⁻¹ = 1/7.
The question calls the altitude CF, but the figure and the question’s last line call it CE. The key (B) is right.
The Kannada prints 9n + 9n + 9n for 9ⁿ + 9ⁿ + 9ⁿ. The key (B) is right.
